report: The patient has cough, dyspnea, chest pain, brain/bone metastases, and multiple prior treatment lines. CT shows a lung lesion with pleural effusion and follow-up enlargement with increased pulmonary nodules. Pathologist and radiologist favor metastatic deposits. NGS and treatment history exclude a new primary or treatment-related injury; no infection evidence. Pulmonary embolism is less likely; imaging refutes it, though definitive testing is unavailable. Thus metastatic cancer progression is the most likely diagnosis.
